hints: Focus on the words transcribed and non-transcribed. Which DNA strand is actually read to make mRNA, and which one is left alone?
Remember how the untouched coding strand relates to mRNA. It matches it almost exactly, but what base does DNA use instead of U?
walkthrough:
**Sort out the two DNA strands**

Think of transcription like copying. One strand is read, that is the transcribed or template strand.

The other strand is not read, that is the non-transcribed or coding strand. We want that second one.

**Link the coding strand to mRNA**

The mRNA is built to be complementary to the template, so it ends up as a copy of the coding strand.

The only difference is RNA uses uracil ($U$) where DNA uses thymine ($T$).

**Convert GAU CUG UAA CGG to DNA**

Take the mRNA sequence and simply swap every $U$ for $T$:
$$GAU \rightarrow GAT, \quad CUG \rightarrow CTG, \quad UAA \rightarrow TAA, \quad CGG \rightarrow CGG$$

That gives $GAT$ $CTG$ $TAA$ $CGG$, which is option C.

options.A: This is the transcribed (template) strand. It is complementary to mRNA, not identical to it.
options.B: This contains uracil ($U$), so it cannot be DNA. It is also complementary to the mRNA, not the coding copy.
options.C: This matches the mRNA exactly with $T$ in place of $U$. That is exactly what the non-transcribed coding strand looks like.
options.D: This is the mRNA sequence itself. DNA never contains $U$, it uses $T$ instead.
